newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia buys Russian for air force, army.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia buys Russian for air force, army.

text.p: Indonesia announced on Tuesday it would buy Russian jets and helicopters after cancelling a deal to purchase U.S. F-16 fighters over Congressional attacks on its human rights record.
State Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita told a news conference Indonesia would buy 12 Sukhoi Su-30K fighters and eight MI-17-1V helicopters.
He said the decision was "based on a study and comparison of various helicopters and fighter planes".
The minister added that ideally Indonesia wanted to buy 20 fighters.
"But for the first phase, we decided on eight helicopters and 12 fighter planes. There is a possibility we can buy more in future from Russia," he said.

In June, Indonesia, angered by U.S. Congressional criticism of its human rights record, cancelled a deal to buy nine U.S. F-16 jets. The government also pulled out of a U.S. military education and training programme.
Ginanjar said it now has 10 F-16s from an earlier deal in which it had bought 12. Two are believed to have crashed.
Military analysts said the Russian purchase was a rebuff for the Americans, and Washington was unlikely to make further sales in Indonesia for at least a couple of years.
Indonesia also studied the possibility of buying French Mirage-2000s or Swedish Grippen jets after the F-16 debacle.
Ginanjar said the Indonesian and Russian governments would discuss the price and payment conditions, technology transfers, spare parts and after-sales backup.
He added there was a condition for counter purchases, possibly covering palm oil, coffee and rubber, and this would be the responsibility of the Trade and Industry Ministry.

The Sukhois, which can fly at twice the speed of sound and have a range of some 3,000 km (1,800 miles), are to help upgrade the air force. The helicopters, each capable of carrying 30 people, are expected to be operated by the army's elite Special Forces (Kopassus) which is being increased to more than 5,000 personnel from around 3,000.
Military sources said Special Forces commander Major-General Prabowo Subianto was expected to go to Moscow later this week.
Military analysts said the Russian purchase had been expected, but added that Indonesia would face a problem in integrating the new aircraft within its existing systems.
"The Sukhoi is a capable aircraft, there's no question about that. But the problem is that they are faced with totally different spares, backing and logistics, and flying as well," one analyst said.
Indonesia also has 24 British Hawk jet trainers and fighters, and the new British Labour government recently gave the go ahead for the export of a further 16 Hawks.
It has a squadron of around 12 U.S. F-5 fighters and around 20 U.S. A-4 Skyhawks.

Indonesia, an archipelago of some 17,500 islands sprawling 5,000 km (3,000 miles) along the equator, is also in the market for a full upgrade of its air defence system and overall air traffic control.
Military sources said an air defence system would include ground-based and air radar surveillance, short and long-range anti-aircraft missiles, control centres and interceptor jets.
They said the whole archipelago was also badly in need of an integrated updated air traffic control system to replace the hodge-podge of systems now in use.
